question: I have a scute swarm with 6 lands, a green warden on my battle field and doubling season. If I played 5 lands how many scute swarms would that make?

answer.verdict: 243 Scute Swarms in total: your original plus 242 token copies. The number triples with each land: 1 → 3 → 9 → 27 → 81 → 243.
answer.summary: Because you already control six or more lands, each Scute Swarm's landfall trigger makes a token copy of itself instead of a 1/1 Insect [O1]. That self-replacement is applied first [C8], and then Doubling Season turns each copy into two [O2][C11]. Every token copy has the same landfall ability and can make copies of itself [R4][C9]. So each land you play makes every Swarm you control trigger [R1][R3], and each trigger adds two Swarms, which triples your count.

citations.why: Token copies have the landfall ability and can create copies of themselves.
Landfall creates a token copy instead of an Insect when you control six or more lands.
Doubling Season doubles the tokens created.
Landfall triggers when you play a land.
Every landfall ability you control triggers for each land.
The self-replacement (copy instead of Insect) applies before Doubling Season.
Doubling Season applies to creating token copies.
A copy acquires the original's rules text.

followUps: What if I had two Doubling Seasons?
Does fetching a land with a fetchland also trigger every Swarm?
What happens if I sacrifice lands and drop below six?
assumptions: You start with exactly one Scute Swarm (the original card) and only one Doubling Season.

"Green warden" isn't in the sources I have; I assumed it doesn't create tokens, double anything or add landfall triggers. It might be how you get the extra land drops. If it does something more, the count could change.
You play the five lands one at a time, and each land's triggers resolve before the next land. You can only play a land when the stack is empty, so this is how it normally goes.
Nothing removes any Swarms or counters the triggers during the process.

sources.label: Scute Swarm
sources.text:
Scute Swarm {2}{G} - Creature — Insect
Landfall — Whenever a land you control enters, create a 1/1 green Insect creature token. If you control six or more lands, create a token that's a copy of this creature instead.

sources.label: Doubling Season
sources.text:
Doubling Season {4}{G} - Enchantment
If an effect would create one or more tokens under your control, it creates twice that many of those tokens instead.
If an effect would put one or more counters on a permanent you control, it puts twice that many of those counters on that permanent instead.

sources.label: Ruling: Scute Swarm
sources.text: A landfall ability triggers whenever a land you control enters for any reason. It triggers whenever you play a land, as well as whenever a spell or ability puts a land onto the battlefield under your control.

sources.label: Ruling: Scute Swarm
sources.text: A landfall ability doesn't trigger if a permanent already on the battlefield becomes a land.

sources.label: Ruling: Scute Swarm
sources.text: Whenever a land you control enters, each landfall ability of the permanents you control will trigger. You can put them   on the stack in any order. The last ability you put on the stack will be the first one to resolve (As a result, you can have those abilities resolve in the order of your choosing.).

sources.label: Ruling: Scute Swarm
sources.text: The token copy will have Scute Swarm's ability. It will also be able to create copies of itself.

sources.label: Ruling: Scute Swarm
sources.text: The token copy won't copy counters or damage marked on Scute Swarm, nor will it copy other effects that have changed Scute Swarm's power, toughness, types, color, and so on. Normally, this means the token will simply be a Scute Swarm, but if any copy effects have affected the original Scute Swarm, the token will take those into account.

sources.label: Ruling: Scute Swarm
sources.text: If Scute Swarm leaves the battlefield before its triggered ability resolves, the token will still enter the battlefield as a copy of Scute Swarm, using Scute Swarm's copiable values from when it was last on the battlefield.

sources.label: Ruling: Doubling Season
sources.text: Planeswalkers will enter with double the normal number of loyalty counters. However, if you activate an ability whose cost has you put loyalty counters on a planeswalker, the number you put on isn't doubled. This is because those counters are put on as a cost, not as an effect.

sources.label: Ruling: Doubling Season
sources.text: Everything that is specified by the effect creating the original token or tokens will also be true about the additional token or tokens created by Doubling Season's replacement effect. For example, if an effect tells you to create a token "tapped and attacking," the additional tokens will also be tapped and attacking.

sources.label: Ruling: Doubling Season
sources.text: Doubling Season affects permanents that enter with counters.

sources.label: Ruling: Doubling Season
sources.text: Battles will enter with double the normal number of defense counters.

sources.label: Ruling: Doubling Season
sources.text: If there are two Doubling Seasons on the battlefield, then the number of tokens or counters is four times the original number. If there are three on the battlefield, then the number of tokens or counters is eight times the original number, and so on.

sources.label: Glossary: Replacement Effect
sources.text: A kind of continuous effect that watches for a particular event that would happen and completely or partially replaces that event with a different event. See rule 614, “Replacement Effects.”

sources.label: CR 614.15
sources.text:
Some replacement effects are not continuous effects. Rather, they are an effect of a resolving spell or ability that replace part or all of that spell or ability’s own effect(s). Such effects are called self-replacement effects. The text creating a self-replacement effect is usually part of the ability whose effect is being replaced, but the text can be a separate ability, particularly when preceded by an ability word. When applying replacement effects to an event, self-replacement effects are applied before other replacement effects.
[Included because: replacement effect]
